exposure: Vertical transmission of bacteria from mother to infant
outcome: Transmission and persistence of microbial strains
cohort: The study included infants and their family members from whom fecal metagenomes were collected to track microbial strains.
finding: The infant gut is selectively seeded by maternal bacterial strains (Actinobacteria and Bacteroidia) that persist for at least 1 year, forming a stable community, with later and ongoing influx of strains from the family environment into adulthood.
mod_finding: Caesarean-born infants show a striking lack of maternal strain transmission at birth compared to vaginally born infants.
